correctness.rationale: All 2^16 complementary-output feedback rules are checked, with an explicit proof that every order-five binary de Bruijn cycle uniquely determines a rule that is one 32-state cycle. Independently, unrestricted Euler-tour enumeration on the 4-bit de Bruijn graph returns precisely the same 2,048 cycles. The 65,536 cuts are checked by two independent integer formulas for aperiodic autocorrelation (bipolar-product sum versus 32-t minus twice mismatches), agreeing exactly. The Python checker was replayed successfully from its actual packaged path. Finite counts are only asserted for this finite family; no extrapolation occurs.

value.rationale: Aperiodic peak sidelobe level is an operationally motivated digital-sequence quality criterion; order-five de Bruijn cycles form a natural complete family with optimal contiguous-word coverage. The classification quantifies all admissible phase choices and the sharp achievable tradeoff within that family, including 40 level-four phases of 32 cycles and eight cycles whose best phase is level sixteen. This complete finite cutoff has exact design and benchmark value not furnished by periodic correlation summaries, independently of unproved higher-order conjectures.
